attributes.source_locator: Section 6 'Loop redesign'; Figure 12; Appendix G 'Loop and window redesign and named enzymes'
attributes.value: Loop redesign. HyInv redesigns loop windows of 16 to 25 residues in a fixed context, with the window within 0.5 to 1.8 Angstrom of the experimental structure; the three displayed cases are 9T2I (178 aa, window of 25, scTM 0.97, window RMSD 1.3 to 1.8 Angstrom), 10UT (156 aa, window of 16, scTM 0.99, 0.5 to 0.7 Angstrom) and 9SNE (172 aa, window of 20, scTM 0.96, 0.6 to 0.7 Angstrom), each the four highest-scTM designs of 128. The panel is 8 backbones chosen by rule plus 4 named enzymes, 128 designs per backbone and region, 24,672 designs in all; a design succeeds if its whole-chain scTM is at least 0.9 and the region CA RMSD after fitting the unchanged context is at most 1.5 Angstrom, and the success rate is read only where the native refold meets the criterion on a majority of backbones. No success rate is printed as a cell.

attributes.source_locator: Section 6 'Pocket-constrained libraries'; Figure 10 panels a and c; Appendix G 'Pocket-constrained libraries'
attributes.value: Pocket-constrained libraries. With the 15 ligand-contacting residues of a 148-residue binder fixed (backbone 9NZE, ligand A1B7L), 373 of 384 designs pass on that one backbone, which the report says is shown for display; the mean pass rate over twelve pocket backbones is 43%. A design passes if its scTM is at least 0.90 and its site CA RMSD at most 1.0 Angstrom. The five displayed designs have scTM 0.98 to 0.99, pocket RMSD 0.37 to 0.73 Angstrom and 41 to 50% pairwise identity. The panel is 12 backbones, ten chosen by rule and two single cases chosen earlier, with 384 designs per backbone and cell; the endpoint is the number of distinct sequences after clustering at 50% identity among the passing designs of a plate, against ProteinMPNN at the temperature whose diversity at the free positions is closest to HyInv's. Retention of the pinned residues is a check of the code and not a result.

attributes.source_locator: Appendix G 'Predictors, comparators and statistics'
attributes.value: For the application tasks, monomers are folded with ESMFold2 with one fold seed shared by all generators for the same backbone and chunk, so generators are paired, and a subset of cells is also folded with Boltz2 and Protenix2. Comparators are ProteinMPNN and ProteinZero V2 only. The diversity-matched baseline temperature is chosen from sequences alone, before any fold is read, as the grid value whose mean pairwise Hamming distance over the designed positions is closest to HyInv's; where HyInv has lower diversity than the lowest baseline temperature the match is as close as the grid allows. Differences are paired by backbone, averaged over designs first, with 95% percentile intervals from 10,000 resamples, and the report notes that with four to twelve backbones the intervals are wide. Intervals are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

attributes.source_locator: Appendix D.1, D.2 and D.3; Appendix A 'Scores at equal diversity'; Section 5.2
attributes.value: The ten baselines are single published settings at one temperature each, not tuned to the panels, so comparisons are at comparable rather than exactly equal diversity. Of the 70 comparisons (ten baselines in seven panel-predictor columns) all 70 point estimates favour HyInv and 61 have an interval that excludes zero; the nine that include zero are ProteinMPNN (TS500, TS50), ProteinMPNN grouped (TS50), ProteinZero V2 ESM1 (CATH4.3 test, TS500, TS50), ProteinZero V2 ESM2 (CATH4.3 test, TS50) and LigandMPNN (TS50). PiFold, CMLM, LM-Design and DPLM-2 3B are single points at much lower diversity than HyInv, so their differences are not at matched diversity. ProteinMPNN is the only baseline with a temperature sweep, and it is the only baseline for which the report reads an equal-diversity difference. HyInv's diversity is above ProteinMPNN with a clear interval on CATH4.3 test and CATH4.2 test and above ProteinZero V2 (ESM2) on the same two panels, but 0.015 below ProteinZero V2 (ESM2) on RecentPDB; at the development curve's slope of 0.07 scTM per unit of diversity the report puts the largest offset (0.016) at a worth of at most 0.0011 scTM.

attributes.value: Six panels. attributes.value: ESMFold2 is the primary structure predictor and also the reinforcement-learning reward predictor, so RecentPDB is folded in addition by Boltz2 and Protenix2, which never enter training. attributes.source_locator: Section 2.1 'Architecture'; Appendix C 'Configuration'; AI4Science/hyinv/README.md opening paragraph
attributes.value: A message-passing graph network with 1,957,573 parameters following the encoder-decoder design of ProteinMPNN: width 128, 4 encoder layers and 3 decoder layers, each residue connected to its 48 nearest neighbours with rotation- and translation-invariant distance and orientation features, random initialisation. The encoder runs once per backbone; the decoder predicts amino acid distributions at masked positions from the backbone and the observed sequence context. At inference the model needs neither a protein language model, a structure predictor nor an alignment.

attributes.value: Latencies were measured on one NVIDIA H20 (Hopper class, sm_90) of a node on which nothing else ran, with PyTorch 2.7.1 and CUDA 12.9. The timed region excludes model loading, CUDA graph capture and kernel compilation; a first call costs 67.7 ms to 834 ms per shape bucket in the report's accounting, and the package README puts cold-cache Triton compilation at about 25 s for the exact path and 14 s for the BF16 path, plus about 0.1 to 0.2 s to capture a graph for a new shape. The kernels were verified on an H20 only and have not been verified on other architectures. HyInv's timing rows used the supervised-stage weights and a rewrite temperature of 0.23, not the released checkpoint's default. Baselines ran with their released implementations in FP32 without graph capture or compilation, DPLM-2 3B in BF16 autocast, and unbatched where the released adapter handles one structure per call, so the report states the speed-ups are against those implementations and not against the best achievable speed of the baseline models.

attributes.source_locator: Appendix F 'The two numerical paths'; Section 4 'Quality'; AI4Science/hyinv/README.md 'Accelerated inference'
attributes.value: Two accelerated paths. The exact FP32 path computes matrix products by a three-pass TF32 emulation of FP32 with erf GELU and returns the reference sampler's sequences for the same seeds (1,600 of 1,600 eager, 400 of 400 with graph capture, 352 of 352 in padded multi-target batches), with graph replay equal to eager execution bit for bit; the report calls only this path identical. The BF16 path uses BF16 operands with FP32 accumulation and tanh GELU and is a numerically different path: against the reference on 200 development backbones the largest absolute logit difference is 0.069, the mean KL divergence per sampled position 5.2e-5 (99th percentile 7.5e-4), the argmax agrees at 99.73% of positions and, with the same seeds, 49.4% of sequences are identical and 98.7% of positions agree. All sequences scored in Section 5 come from the reference sampler.

attributes.source_locator: Sections 3.1 and 3.2; Appendix E 'Procedure and groups' and 'Random streams, truncation and fixed residues'; AI4Science/hyinv/README.md opening paragraph
attributes.value: Deployment samples in 16 decoder passes after one encoder pass: the positions are split at random into 8 fixed equal-size groups, 8 rounds of blind drafting at temperature 0.6 sample one group each from the all-masked state, then 8 rounds of rewriting at temperature 0.34 mask and resample one group at a time with all other positions visible. The group permutation is drawn from a SHA-256 hash of the seed and the chain identifier and is independent of structure, sequence and weights. Truncation at inference uses top-p 0.9 and min-p 0.1. Fixed residues are visible as the native residue from the first round and are redrawn unchanged at every stage.

attributes.source_locator: Table 4 'Training configuration'; Appendix C 'Reward and stability proxy' and 'RL objective'
attributes.value: Two stages. Supervised: 627,945 structures, random-order likelihood objective, 85,000 updates, windows up to 512, AdamW with beta (0.9, 0.98), a Noam learning-rate schedule and label smoothing 0.1. Reinforcement learning: 50,000 backbones, a reward with a leave-one-out advantage over 32 candidates per backbone, 640 updates of a 656-update run, batches of 256 backbones by 32 candidates, AdamW with beta (0.9, 0.95), a constant learning rate of 2e-5, a KL penalty of 0.005 then 0.001 to the fixed supervised checkpoint, and sampling at temperature 0.3. The reward is scTM computed with ESMFold2 and TM-align; a ProteinMPNN-derived bounded likelihood contrast supplies five percent of it as a model-derived stability proxy, which the report states is not a stability measurement. Native sequence recovery has weight zero.

attributes.source_locator: Appendix C 'Data and pool', third and fourth bullets; Appendix G 'Homology of the panels'; Table 10
attributes.value: The authors state: 'We do not claim zero sequence overlap between the training data and the evaluation panels.' The reinforcement-learning pool was filtered against the benchmark panels with a same-source homology mask built from MMseqs2 searches of the candidate records against the benchmark sequences, excluding a record if it is positive under the mask and using a record only if that search queried it; the supervised corpus was filtered by exact-sequence removal and a homology filter. For the application panels Appendix G's screen is a coverage rule: a hit counts only if its identity is at least 0.3 and it covers at least 0.8 of the query or of the target, so partial hits remain, and the report says a backbone passing the rule is homology-filtered at these thresholds, 'which is weaker than having no similar fragment in the library'.

name: ProteinZero V2 (ESM2) on TS500 (CA-lDDT of designed sequences under ESMFold2, HyInv report)

comparison.adaptation: HyInv runs its default setting. ProteinMPNN and ProteinZero V2 are interpolated at the HyInv diversity from their temperature grids, without extrapolating by more than 0.05, so the comparison is at matched diversity
comparison.aggregation: Mean number of qualifying designs per backbone over the 74 backbones; the resampling unit is the cluster of 30% identity.
comparison.dataset_version: As assembled for the HyInv technical report (2026-10-14); no chain list or split manifest is published
comparison.inputs: Backbone N, CA, C and O coordinates of the panel chain; no sequence, alignment, language model or structure predictor at design time
comparison.metric_implementation: 74 de novo backbones, 4 designs each. A design is foldable if its ESMFold2 scTM is at least 0.9 and novel if its identity to the nearest UniRef50 sequence and to the nearest pretraining-library sequence is below 0.3. The composition filter keeps sequences with entropy at least 3.5 bits, hydrophobic fraction (AVILMFWY) between 0.25 and 0.55 and longest homopolymer run at most 6, which excludes low-complexity sequences a structure predictor can fold to a high scTM. Both readings were fixed before designs were generated. HyInv is compared with ProteinMPNN and ProteinZero V2 over their temperature grids, interpolating each curve at the HyInv diversity without extrapolating by more than 0.05.
comparison.population: 74 de novo backbones in 58 clusters of 30% sequence identity, none with a hit that passes the report's homology rule; 28 have partial hits below the coverage limit (Table 10)

comparison.aggregation: Designs of a target averaged first, then a macro-average over the chains of the panel. A failed fold is a gap in the average, not imputed.

comparison.metric_implementation: TM-align (Zhang and Skolnick 2005) of the ESMFold2 prediction against the native CA trace at valid sites. Fold seeds on the public panels with K = 2 designs per chain are the seeds recorded with the baseline samples, so comparisons with baseline sequences share the folding randomness.
comparison.population: Test split of CATH 4.2 as used by Ingraham et al. 2019, 1,120 chains in 109 CATH topology clusters.

attributes.aggregation: Median of 11 repeats (headline cells), 7 (sweeps) or 3 (slow systems of the library cells) after 3 warm-up calls; the interquartile range is below 1% of the median in every ladder row.
limitations: Appendix F states that where a released adapter handles one structure per call, 128 designs are 128 calls, so a batched reimplementation of the baseline would be faster; the measured times are of those released implementations and not of the best achievable speed of the baseline models.
HyInv's rows were timed with the supervised-stage weights and a rewrite temperature of 0.23, not with the released checkpoint at its default temperatures.
DPLM-2 3B decodes by argmax, so every call returns the same sequence and its time is that of producing 128 designs scaled from eight timed calls.
One GPU model (NVIDIA H20, Hopper class) on one node; no other hardware was timed.
Compilation and CUDA graph capture are excluded from the timed region, so a first call in practice costs more than the printed figure.
attributes.metric_implementation: PyTorch 2.7.1, CUDA 12.9, TF32 for matrix products off unless stated, on one NVIDIA H20 of a node on which nothing else ran. The timed region starts at host arrays and ends at the sampled tokens on the device: upload, backbone batch, encoder and structure terms and all 16 decoder passes of every candidate batch, but not model loading, graph capture or kernel compilation (first call 67.7 ms to 834 ms per shape bucket). Every call draws fresh seeds and nothing is cached across calls. HyInv rows were timed with the supervised-stage weights and a rewrite temperature of 0.23. Baselines ran with their released implementations in FP32 without graph capture or compilation, DPLM-2 3B in BF16 autocast, each at its published setting.
attributes.metric_qualifier: Median wall-clock time of one design request on one NVIDIA H20, 128 candidates per request with a maximum candidate batch of 32 unless the request is the 10,000-design library; the timed region excludes model loading, CUDA graph capture and kernel compilation; the backbone length is named per result

attributes.metric_implementation: 74 de novo backbones, 4 designs each. A design is foldable if its ESMFold2 scTM is at least 0.9 and novel if its identity to the nearest UniRef50 sequence and to the nearest pretraining-library sequence is below 0.3. The composition filter keeps sequences with entropy at least 3.5 bits, hydrophobic fraction (AVILMFWY) between 0.25 and 0.55 and longest homopolymer run at most 6, which excludes low-complexity sequences a structure predictor can fold to a high scTM. Both readings were fixed before designs were generated. HyInv is compared with ProteinMPNN and ProteinZero V2 over their temperature grids, interpolating each curve at the HyInv diversity without extrapolating by more than 0.05.

attributes.aggregation: Difference of fitted values, paired; 95% percentile interval over CATH topology clusters, over chains on RecentPDB.
limitations: Measured on the checkpoint at update 288, not on the released update-640 checkpoint.
The draft temperature was chosen on the development panel, so the report treats the held-out confirmation on CATH4.3 test and RecentPDB as the evidence for the gain.
This compares two settings of HyInv itself; it says nothing about any baseline.
attributes.metric_implementation: A sampler family is evaluated at a grid of rewrite temperatures, giving points of diversity and scTM on the same chains. The scTM at fixed diversity D is the value at D of the least-squares quadratic fit s = a + b*d + c*d^2, with no extrapolation. The gain of a setting is its S@D minus that of the unmodified sampler of the same checkpoint on the same panel, with an interval from 1,000 draws in which all points of all curves are recomputed from one cluster resample. Grids: {0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7} for the unmodified sampler, {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.5} for the decoupled sampler at Td = 0.6 and {0.3, 0.4, 0.5, 0.7} at Td = 0.3. On the held-out panels D is the development value times the ratio of the panel to the development diversity of the unmodified sampler. Development chains K = 2, held-out panels K = 4 with new draws and fold seeds.
attributes.metric_qualifier: Setting minus the unmodified single-temperature sampler of the same checkpoint on the same panel, both read at fixed diversity (D = 0.30 on the development panel, 0.32 on CATH4.3 test, 0.30 on RecentPDB), paired, with a 95% interval; ESMFold2; checkpoint at update 288; the reference system is the unmodified sampler
attributes.protocol: Measure how much a sampler setting raises scTM over the unmodified single-temperature sampler of the same checkpoint when both are read at the same diversity.

attributes.version: HyInv technical report, 2026-10-14

attributes.aggregation: Difference of the HyInv point and the fitted ProteinMPNN curve; 95% intervals over clusters.
limitations: ProteinMPNN is the only baseline with a temperature grid, so this equal-diversity reading exists for ProteinMPNN alone and cannot be extended to the other nine baselines.
Two of ProteinMPNN's three temperatures were generated for this report rather than taken from its published setting.

attributes.metric_implementation: Figure 16 places every method in the scTM-diversity plane of each panel. attributes.aggregation: Designs of a target averaged first, then a macro-average over the 121 chains.
limitations: Baselines run at one published temperature each, so their design-set diversity is not matched to HyInv's: Appendix D.2 states that PiFold, CMLM, LM-Design and DPLM-2 3B are single points at much lower diversity than HyInv and that their differences are not at matched diversity. attributes.aggregation: Macro-average over the chains of the panel.

attributes.metric_implementation: D = 2/(K(K-1)) * sum over design pairs of the normalised Hamming distance over valid sites (Appendix A, equation 2). The report gives ProteinMPNN on CATH4.3 test as 0.290 at all sites against 0.314 at valid sites.
attributes.metric_qualifier: Mean pairwise normalised Hamming distance between the K designs of a chain over valid sites, then a macro-average over targets; counted at valid sites for every method, because baseline sequences carry X at invalid sites and counting those as identical would lower their diversity

evidence_concerns.message: Appendix C states 'We do not claim zero sequence overlap between the training data and the evaluation panels', and Appendix G's homology screen is a coverage rule under which partial hits remain (Table 10: 28 of 74 de novo backbones and 7 of 12 pocket backbones have partial hits, and all 4 named enzymes are homologous to training data by design). Results on these panels are therefore not clean held-out measurements and must not be compared with results from sources that do establish no overlap.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Appendix C 'Data and pool', final bullet; Appendix G 'Homology of the panels' and Table 10

evidence_concerns.message: The ten baselines are single published settings at one temperature each, so their design-set diversity differs from HyInv's: on CATH4.3 test HyInv samples at diversity 0.331 against 0.093 for PiFold, 0.104 for CMLM, 0.144 for LM-Design 650M and 0.000 for DPLM-2 3B, which decodes by argmax. Appendix D.2 states that these four differences are not at matched diversity, and Appendix A states that even for the closest baselines the comparisons are 'close to, but not exactly at, equal diversity', the largest offset of 0.016 being worth at most 0.0011 scTM at the development slope. The scTM and scTM difference results of the protocols named here must not be read as a matched-diversity ranking. The results read at a stated diversity level (Tables 8 and 9 and Appendix D.3) are not covered by this entry, because they are the ones the report reads on a fitted curve at a fixed diversity; nor are the recovery, diversity, pLDDT, scRMSD and lDDT results, whose protocols carry the same single-setting caveat in their own limitations and whose metric qualifiers say the value is at each method's own setting.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Appendix D.1 and D.2; Table 7; Figure 14 diversity block; Section 5.1 'Baselines' and 'HyInv'

evidence_concerns.message: The inference-time results were measured with the supervised-stage weights and a rewrite temperature of 0.23, not with the released checkpoint and its default temperatures, and the quality read-outs of the two numerical paths used the RL checkpoint at update 288, not update 640. Speed and quality in this report are therefore measured on different weights, and the 57x figure compares HyInv's optimised BF16 path with ProteinMPNN's released implementation rather than with an equally optimised baseline.
evidence_concerns.source_locator: Table 1 footnote; Appendix F 'Timing protocol' and 'Baseline timings'

attributes.extraction_method: pdftotext -layout text layer, parsed by extract/parse.py with every row label and column count asserted.
limitations: Author-released report, not peer reviewed and not independently refereed. All three authors are at Tencent Hunyuan, which released the model, and the baselines were run by the same team.

Every quantity is computed on predicted structures and designed sequences. Appendix B states that none is an experimental measurement, so no binding, stability or activity is measured anywhere in the report.

Appendix C states: 'We do not claim zero sequence overlap between the training data and the evaluation panels.' The RL pool was filtered against the panels with a same-source homology mask and the supervised corpus by exact-sequence removal and a homology filter, which is weaker than no overlap.

The ten baselines are each at one published single-temperature setting and were not tuned to the panels, so the scTM comparisons are at comparable rather than equal sequence diversity. Appendix D.2 states that PiFold, CMLM, LM-Design and DPLM-2 3B are single points at much lower diversity than HyInv.

ESMFold2 is both the primary scoring predictor and the reinforcement-learning reward, so the five ESMFold2 panels favour the trained model by construction; only RecentPDB is also folded by Boltz2 and Protenix2.

Some baseline ESMFold2 cells were regenerated for the report rather than taken from the released scores (Table 5), and the ProteinMPNN temperatures other than the published one were generated for the report.

Appendix A records run-to-run noise of about +/-0.0015 scTM per panel and says differences between checkpoints below about 0.003 are not resolvable; intervals are not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

Latencies were measured on one NVIDIA H20 and exclude model loading, CUDA graph capture and kernel compilation. Baselines ran as released, unbatched where the released adapter handles one structure per call, so Appendix F states the speed-ups are against those implementations and not against the best achievable speed of the baseline models.

Figures 1, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9b, 11c, 13, 16 and 17 carry results that are not printed as labelled cells, or whose bar order cannot be recovered from the text layer; they are recorded as gaps in notes.md, not read by eye.
